name: KOR-Bench
abstract: KOR-Bench evaluates knowledge-orthogonal reasoning by reducing the effect of prior domain knowledge. This page uses the Overall score from the main results table.
contributions: The benchmark aims to separate actual reasoning ability from memorized knowledge.
The page uses the main Overall score and does not mix in the additional integrated-task setting.
method: KOR-Bench introduces the idea of knowledge-orthogonal reasoning, aiming to evaluate rule understanding and reasoning ability while minimizing dependence on domain-specific knowledge.
It includes five task families: operation, logic, cipher, puzzle, and counterfactual, all designed around novel rule-driven problems.
The paper shows that this benchmark can better reveal whether a model is genuinely reasoning instead of leaning on memorized knowledge patterns.
It also studies stepwise prompting, self-correction, and task-specific tricks, making KOR-Bench a useful foundation for general reasoning evaluation.
leaderboard_note: The primary leaderboard uses Overall from the main table. The paper also reports integrated-task analyses such as Multi-Q / Multi-R / Multi-RQ, which are not mixed into the main leaderboard.
